description: The word an agent row says about an agent's state, on every surface that says it. The project service derives it once in derive_session_semantics as presentation.statusLabel; the TUI renders that string verbatim and the Expo app renders it sentence-cased. The app used to compute its own word from `status` and said "Running" for an agent the service had already called `ready` -- an agent that had finished its turn and was sitting at an empty prompt. The status dot next to that word was right the whole time, which is what makes this a one-answer-many-surfaces failure rather than a wrong rule.

cases.why: the case Sam reported: process alive, turn finished, sitting at an empty prompt
waiting on a tool, which is work and not an ask
waiting on a reply to something it sent; the app called this "Needs reply" while every other surface said "needs answer"
blocked on something it cannot clear itself
finished a turn and reported done, which is not the same as idle
idle with no activity recorded at all

exited.why: The one place the app shows detail the shared word drops. runtime_lifecycle folds `exited` into `offline`, so statusLabel says `offline`, while the TUI's own row still says "Exited". Pinned so that moving the distinction into the shared label is a deliberate change to this fixture rather than a silent divergence.
